subQuestions.questionText: A plan used to make a journey logical and timesaving:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
Route plan — a route plan maps out a logical, time-saving journey between destinations.

subQuestions.questionText: A … itinerary is designed according to a tourist's needs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
personalised — a personalised itinerary is tailored to the individual needs of a tourist.

subQuestions.questionText: Tourists are vulnerable to crime-related incidents. As a safety precaution at the airport, tourists must …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
ensure luggage is securely locked — locking luggage protects belongings and reduces the risk of theft or tampering at the airport.

subQuestions.questionText: Preventative advice given by travel clinics to tourists travelling to destinations with extremely high temperatures:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Use sunscreen containing a high sun protection factor — high-SPF sunscreen protects against harsh sun in extremely hot destinations.

options.A: Take hot showers to keep cool.
options.B: Consume sugary drinks to keep hydrated.
options.C: Wear reading glasses for protection against the harsh sunlight.
options.D: Use sunscreen containing a high sun protection factor.

subQuestions.questionText: A document required when obtaining an international driving permit (IDP):
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
Valid South African driving licence — a valid national driving licence is required to obtain an International Driving Permit.

subQuestions.questionText: The Berlin Wall was built to divide this country into west and east:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Germany — the Berlin Wall divided Germany into West and East.

subQuestions.questionText: The statue of Christ The Redeemer and the Vatican City have the following in common: Both …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
have religious significance — both the statue of Christ the Redeemer and the Vatican City are Christian religious landmarks.

subQuestions.questionText: The Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa consist of three sites called the Makapan Valley, the Taung Skull Fossil Site and the …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Cradle of Humankind — it is one of the three Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa alongside Makapan Valley and Taung Skull Fossil Site.

subQuestions.questionText: The Vredefort Dome World Heritage Site meets this UNESCO criterion:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Geological evidence of a meteorite impact structure — the Vredefort Dome is the site of the world's largest verified meteorite impact.

options.A: Biological evidence of human developmental stages
options.B: Geological evidence of a meteorite impact structure
options.C: An outstanding example of a human settlement
options.D: An outstanding example of a unique type of building

subQuestions.questionText: Marketing South Africa internationally will lead to a/an …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
increase in tourist volumes — effective international marketing attracts more visitors, increasing tourist volumes.

subQuestions.questionText: This factor contributes to the professional image of an employee working in the tourism industry:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Positive interaction with customers — engaging positively with customers builds a professional image in the tourism industry.

subQuestions.questionText: A reason why people may want to apply for jobs in the airline industry:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
They will enjoy fringe benefits such as discounted travel — discounted travel is a common fringe benefit that attracts people to airline industry jobs.

options.A: They will enjoy fringe benefits such as discounted travel.
options.B: Everyone will earn above average salaries.
options.C: They will automatically become shareholders in the airline.

subQuestions.questionText: The image shows internet-based platforms where tourism businesses have an online presence. These platforms are known as … (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
social media — internet-based platforms where businesses maintain an online presence are known as social media.

subQuestions.questionText: This document guides staff on the expected behaviour in the performance of their duties and staff members faced with ethical challenges:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Code of conduct — a code of conduct guides staff behaviour and helps them handle ethical challenges at work.

options.A: Basic Conditions of Employment Act, 1997 (Act 75 of 1997)
options.C: The King III report on sustainability

subQuestions.questionText: The manner in which a company presents its products to customers, which will contribute to a professional image:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Packaging design — the way products are packaged and presented to customers contributes to a professional image.

subQuestions.questionText: The year 2020 had unprecedented (never experienced before) political and social uprisings. This type of occurrence is referred to as a …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
protest action — political and social uprisings are classified as protest action.

subQuestions.questionText: A negative impact of Covid-19 on major soccer events:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Soccer stadiums were empty — Covid-19 restrictions meant spectators were not allowed, leaving stadiums empty.

subQuestions.questionText: Participating countries took this decision to prevent the spread of Covid-19 during the World Economic Forum (WEF) in January 2021:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
The WEF was held by means of a virtual platform — holding the event virtually prevented the spread of Covid-19.

options.A: The WEF was held by means of a virtual platform.
options.B: All participants wore masks during the virtual WEF.
options.C: Countries flew their delegates to the WEF.
options.D: Many countries did not participate in the WEF.

subQuestions.questionText: African land markets refer to inbound tourists arriving …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
through South Africa's border posts — African land markets are inbound tourists who arrive overland via South Africa's border posts.

subQuestions.questionText: An example of an electronic customer feedback tool:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Liking a Facebook post on a business' web page — this is an electronic (online) form of customer feedback.

options.A: Writing in a guest journal at a hotel
options.B: Dropping a note in a suggestion box
options.C: Speaking to the manager of the business
options.D: Liking a Facebook post on a business' web page

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE travel document for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: A tourist will need this document to do sightseeing at a stopover city en route to the final-destination country.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: transit visa (1 mark)
A transit visa allows a tourist to stop over and do limited sightseeing in a country en route to the final destination.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE travel document for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: This document for tourists provides evidence of vaccination against yellow fever.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: health certificate (1 mark)
A health certificate provides proof of vaccination, such as against yellow fever, required for entry into certain countries.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE travel document for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: This document issued by the Department of Home Affairs allows South Africans to travel internationally.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: passport (1 mark)
A passport is issued by the Department of Home Affairs and is required for international travel.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE travel document for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: Countries would require these results from tourists travelling internationally during the 2020–2021 global pandemic.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Covid-19 test (1 mark)
Proof of a Covid-19 test result was required by many countries during the 2020–2021 pandemic.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE travel document for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list: This document may be required to allow certain countries entrance to Europe.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Schengen Visa (1 mark)
A Schengen Visa permits entry into the Schengen Area of European countries.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s): Good (environmental/social) practices include resource and waste management.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: environmental (1 mark)
Resource and waste management are environmental practices.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s): The responsible attitude of a tourism business towards the people and environment it affects, is referred to as (CSI/GDP).
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: CSI (1 mark)
Corporate Social Investment (CSI) reflects a business's responsible attitude towards the people and environment it affects.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s): Tourism companies that conduct business in a sustainable manner may be certified by (FTT/TGCSA).
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: FTT (1 mark)
Fair Trade Tourism (FTT) certifies tourism companies that operate sustainably.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s): (Environmentally/Politically)-conscious tourists support businesses who subscribe to the three pillars of the TBL.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Environmentally (1 mark)
Environmentally-conscious tourists support businesses that follow the three pillars of the Triple Bottom Line (TBL).

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s): The procurement of local goods and services by tourism companies contributes to (wellness programmes/economic growth) in the local area.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: economic growth (1 mark)
Buying local goods and services channels money into the local area, contributing to economic growth.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term in Column B that matches the basic condition of employment in Column A: The salary an employee receives for work done. (Column B options: A. working hours; B. core duties; C. remuneration; D. deductions; E. termination of service; F. grooming; G. uniform allowances)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: C / remuneration (1 mark)
Remuneration is the salary or payment an employee receives for work done.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term in Column B that matches the basic condition of employment in Column A: A contribution made by an employer so that an employee appears presentable at work, according to the business policy. (Column B options: A. working hours; B. core duties; C. remuneration; D. deductions; E. termination of service; F. grooming; G. uniform allowances)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: G / uniform allowances (1 mark)
Uniform allowances are contributions from the employer to help staff appear presentable at work.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term in Column B that matches the basic condition of employment in Column A: The decision made by a business when employees are no longer required to fulfil their duties. (Column B options: A. working hours; B. core duties; C. remuneration; D. deductions; E. termination of service; F. grooming; G. uniform allowances)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: E / termination of service (1 mark)
Termination of service is the ending of employment when employees are no longer required.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term in Column B that matches the basic condition of employment in Column A: The contractual time an employee must be present at the place of employment. (Column B options: A. working hours; B. core duties; C. remuneration; D. deductions; E. termination of service; F. grooming; G. uniform allowances)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A / working hours (1 mark)
Working hours are the contractual times an employee must be present at the workplace.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a term in Column B that matches the basic condition of employment in Column A: The key responsibilities of an employee while at work. (Column B options: A. working hours; B. core duties; C. remuneration; D. deductions; E. termination of service; F. grooming; G. uniform allowances)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B / core duties (1 mark)
Core duties are the key responsibilities an employee must perform while at work.

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Xondo won R10 million and will plan his own world trip. Write the FIVE steps of the travel planning process in the CORRECT logical order. The steps (in no particular order) are: Buy a flight ticket/Book accommodation; Do research on the countries to be visited; Apply for a visa; Buy foreign currency; Decide on the travel period.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each step in the correct order (5 marks):
STEP 1 — Do research on the countries to be visited
STEP 2 — Decide on the travel period
STEP 3 — Buy a flight ticket / Book accommodation
STEP 4 — Apply for a visa
STEP 5 — Buy foreign currency
Note: STEP 1 and STEP 2 can be interchanged.

subQuestions.questionText: From the case study 'World Health Organisation and TikTok Join Forces', state the World Health Organisation's main role in the Covid-19 pandemic.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the main role (any of the following):
• The WHO is working to contain the spread of the virus.
• They advise people on measures to take to protect themselves from the virus.
• They direct people to the organisation's website and social media platforms for additional information on the virus.

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO social media platforms (apart from TikTok) that the World Health Organisation is using to update the global nation on the virus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each correct platform (2 x 2 = 4 marks). Any TWO of:
• Google
• Facebook
• Twitter
• Instagram
Note: TikTok is not accepted.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO reasons why the World Health Organisation is confident that joining forces with TikTok will assist in educating the world on the virus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-explained reason (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
• TikTok has a huge, growing audience and is a popular app used by many.
• The audience is mostly Generation Z who can serve as ambassadors to encourage increased action amongst the youth against the virus.
• The volume of users is increasing worldwide so information can reach larger audiences faster.
• The videos are short and easy to follow with no information overload, making it easier to direct a message to the desired audience.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose FOUR duty-free items from the options (A–F) given that Jerome will be permitted to bring into South Africa. Write only the letters. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each correct permitted item (4 marks). Any FOUR of the permitted letters:
• B — Perfume / eau de toilette
• C — Cigarettes
• D — Wine / spirits
• E — Gold bangles to the value of R5 000
• F — Tobacco
Note: Accept any order. (A is prohibited.)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the approved allowances (quantities) for any TWO of the permitted items chosen in QUESTION 2.2.1. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each correct allowance (2 x 2 = 4 marks). Any TWO of:
• B — no more than 50 ml perfume and no more than 250 ml eau de toilette.
• C — no more than 200 cigarettes.
• D — no more than 2 litres of wine per person and no more than 1 litre of spirits.
• F — no more than 250 g of pipe tobacco per person.
• E — new or used goods up to the value of R5 000.

subQuestions.questionText: The items selected in QUESTION 2.2.1 fall within the duty-free allowances. Name the channel Jerome must pass through after collecting his luggage.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Green channel — used by travellers who have nothing to declare / whose goods fall within the duty-free allowances.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.4(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain the term prohibited goods.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the explanation:
• Prohibited goods refer to goods that travellers are not allowed, by law, to bring into a country.
• They are illegal goods that are not allowed to enter a country.
Note: Do not accept examples.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the prohibited item in the pictures. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• A — dynamite / explosives.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the time in Singapore when Mrs Abadi departed from OR Tambo International Airport (+2) at 10:00 on 10 August. Singapore is on +8. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: South Africa +2; Singapore +8
Mark 2: Time difference = 8 − 2 = 6 hours; Singapore is ahead → 10:00 + 6 hours
Mark 3: Time in Singapore = 16:00

Final answer: 16:00

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate Mrs Abadi's time of departure from Changi International Airport (Singapore) on 11 August. The flying time from OR Tambo to Changi was 10 hours and the stopover time at Changi was 4 hours. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Arrival time in Singapore = 16:00 (+) 10 hours flying time
Mark 2: = 02:00
Mark 3: Stopover time = 02:00 (+) 4 hours
Mark 4: Departure time = 06:00

Final answer: 06:00

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate Mrs Abadi's time of arrival at Tullamarine International Airport in Melbourne (+10). She departed Singapore (+8) at 06:00 and the flying time from Singapore to Melbourne was 7 hours. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Singapore +8; Melbourne +10
Mark 2: Time difference = 10 − 8 = 2 hours; Melbourne is ahead → 06:00 + 2 hours
Mark 3: Time in Melbourne = 08:00
Mark 4: Add flying time: 08:00 (+) 7 hours
Mark 5: Arrival time = 15:00

Final answer: 15:00

subQuestions.questionText: Mrs Abadi experienced headaches and exhaustion during the first few days in Melbourne after her long-haul flight. Identify the travel-related condition that Mrs Abadi experienced.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Jet lag.

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend ONE way in which Mrs Abadi could overcome the symptoms of the travel-related condition above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one recommendation (any of the following):
• Get adequate sleep and rest.
• Adjust to the local time.
• Keep hydrated with liquids.
• Avoid caffeinated beverages or alcohol.
• Exercise on the plane.
• Wear loose clothing to facilitate adequate blood circulation.
• Have light meals.
• Take medication to alleviate jet lag symptoms.

subQuestions.questionText: Laila saved R20 000 for her holiday in Los Angeles, USA. Use the exchange rate table (USD: BBR = 15,97; BSR = 16,87) to calculate the amount in US dollars that Laila had saved. Round off your answer to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify correct rate — BSR = 16,87 (used when buying foreign currency)
Mark 2: Calculation: ZAR 20 000 ÷ 16,87
Mark 3: Final answer: USD 1 185,54

Final answer: USD 1 185,54 (rounded to two decimal places)

subQuestions.questionText: Laila had USD 303,50 left to spend and her son chose Jacket A (PRICE: USD 100). Calculate the amount in rand she had left after she had purchased Jacket A. Use the exchange rate table (USD: BBR = 15,97; BSR = 16,87). Round off your answer to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1–2: Amount left in USD = USD 303,50 − USD 100 = USD 203,50
Mark 3: Identify correct rate — BBR = 15,97 (used when converting foreign currency back to rand)
Mark 4: Calculation: USD 203,50 × 15,97
Mark 5: Final answer: ZAR 3 249,90

Final answer: ZAR 3 249,90 (rounded to two decimal places)

subQuestions.questionText: Covid-19 resulted in a steep decline in the South African economy and the GDP dropped to its lowest. Discuss ONE impact of the weakening GDP on the South African economy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one well-discussed impact (any of the following):
• Unemployment leading to a rise in poverty — lessened productivity of goods and services leads to job losses.
• Employees face retrenchments or lower wages, meaning less money to spend on basic needs.
• Investors are less likely to invest in an economy that is not expanding.
• People have less disposable income to spend.
• The country can fall into recession with reduced interest rates and higher inflation, leading to consumer borrowing and greater debt.
• Reversal of the multiplier effect.
• Price increases for goods and services.

subQuestions.label: 4.1.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify icons A to C shown with the statistics. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each correct icon (3 marks):
• A — Niagara Falls
• B — Venice
• C — Sydney Opera House

subQuestions.label: 4.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the continent where EACH of icons A to C is located. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each correct continent (3 marks):
• A — North America
• B — Europe
• C — Australia / Australasia

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the visitor numbers of icon A. Identify the main source market visiting this icon. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Domestic tourists (the majority of the 13 million visitors are domestic).
• Canadians.

subQuestions.questionText: Compare the visitor numbers for icons B and C. Give ONE reason why icon B is more popular than icon C. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one well-explained reason:
• Icon B has visitor numbers for a whole city (Venice), whereas icon C's numbers are for one attraction/icon in the city (Sydney).
• Sydney is a long-haul destination whereas Venice is in close proximity to the countries in Europe.
• Venice is an ancient city with historical significance.
• There are unique attractions in the city built on water.
• Fewer people would go to a harbour (Sydney) than tourists travelling around many attractions in a city (Venice).
• Venice is seen as a romantic city and might have more couples visit compared to Sydney.

subQuestions.label: 4.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: In the case study 'Improving Tourism at an Ancient Site', name the country where the Great Pyramids are located.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark:
• Egypt.

subQuestions.label: 4.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the continent where the Great Pyramids are located.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark:
• Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why the Great Pyramids of Giza are considered a burial site.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one well-explained reason:
• The pyramids were built as tombs for the pharaohs (Egyptian kings).
• The embalmed mummies of the royal and noble families of Egypt were buried here.

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the statement: The body of the Sphinx is in the shape of a …
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• lion.

subQuestions.label: 4.2.4(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The Great Pyramids can be operated as a successful tourist attraction. Discuss TWO examples of how sustainable and responsible management plans are implemented.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-discussed example (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
• Vehicles that might damage the site are left at the visitor centre.
• Traditional camel and horse rides have low impact on the environment and are only allowed in certain areas.
• Electrical vehicles minimise pollution caused by petrol or diesel engines.
• Stalls are allocated in designated areas only.

subQuestions.label: 4.2.4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: The Great Pyramids can be operated as a successful tourist attraction. Discuss TWO examples of how staff behaviour will be efficient and ethical.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-discussed example (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
• Workers and vendors operating their businesses will be trained on providing quality products and excellent service delivery.
• Plans are in place to ensure quality products and services are provided.
• Competitive pricing for local vendors.
• Staff members handle visitors without offending them.
• Many ticket windows speed up ticket sales reserved for a variety of tourist types.
• 18 gift shops minimise over-crowding.

subQuestions.label: 4.2.5(a)
subQuestions.questionText: From the case study, provide evidence that the Great Pyramids cater for both local and international tourists.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the evidence:
• There is a new international airport for international tourists and the road infrastructure has been improved for local visitors.
• There are ticket windows for Egyptian citizens (domestic) and foreigners (international) visiting the site.

subQuestions.label: 4.2.5(b)
subQuestions.questionText: From the case study, provide evidence that the Great Pyramids have a positive impact on the local community.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the evidence (any of the following):
• Craftsmen and traders from the local community have stalls at the site.
• Horse and camel owners are allowed to operate their unusual modes of transport at the Great Pyramids.
• Local community members are photographers that earn money from taking and providing pictures.
• Local drivers are employed to drive the electric vehicles.
• Knowledgeable local members work in the visitor and information centres.
• Entrepreneurship opportunities in the gift shops for local souvenirs.
• Local community members receive training (skills development).
• Improvements in local infrastructure around the Great Pyramids.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the province in which the iSimangaliso Wetland Park is located.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark:
• KwaZulu-Natal / KZN.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct type of World Heritage Site in brackets: iSimangaliso Wetland Park is a (natural/cultural/mixed) World Heritage Site.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark:
• natural.

subQuestions.questionText: Sand that blocked the river and lake from flowing into the sea was removed in January 2021. Name the organisation responsible for World Heritage Sites that might be concerned about the January activities at the iSimangaliso Wetland Park.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• UNESCO / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why the organisation named in QUESTION 5.3.1 will be concerned with these activities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one well-explained reason:
• The status of iSimangaliso Wetland Park as a World Heritage Site could be threatened.
• It was declared a natural site, and human interference (e.g. use of heavy-duty equipment) compromises its natural status.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways in which the removal of the sand to open up the river mouth will benefit the local tourism industry around the iSimangaliso Wetland Park.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-discussed way (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
• More special interest tourists like anglers will come to fish.
• Water-based tourism activities will be able to take place with increased flow of water, marine life and wildlife.
• Ecotourism will increase.
• Lodges and accommodation establishments will receive more visitors.
• It will promote scientific research and training as well as environmental awareness.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the other World Heritage Site located in the same province as the iSimangaliso Wetland Park.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Maloti-Drakensberg Park / uKhahlamba Drakensberg Park.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the organisation responsible for reigniting the local tourism industry through innovative marketing of South Africa as an international destination of choice.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• South African Tourism / SATourism.
Note: Do not accept SAT.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO ways in which the online exhibition 'South Africa: An Explorer's Paradise' will fulfil the core function of coordinating marketing activities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-explained way (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
• Partnerships with industry role-players unify the advertising efforts, and media such as Google Arts and Culture assist in exposing what South Africa has to offer to domestic and international markets.
• The use of the Inspiring New Ways logo provides brand identity to attract more tourists to a recognised destination.
• Bringing together various images, videos, street views and stories shows South Africa's diversity in culture and scenery to the rest of the world.
• Using an online platform connects SATourism's marketing efforts to virtual reality and the global digital world.
• It is a cost-effective platform to market South Africa both domestically and internationally.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify ONE branding strategy on the online page. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one branding strategy:
• South Africa's brand logo.
• Inspiring New Ways slogan.
• Sharing Google Arts and Culture branding — South Africa: An Explorer's Paradise.

subQuestions.questionText: Branding and online marketing are expensive. Discuss ONE way in which the organisation identified in QUESTION 6.1 receives private-sector funding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one well-discussed way:
• TBCSA pays money collected from levy contributors quarterly to SATourism.
• The 1% TOMSA levy is collected by participating tourism businesses from tourists.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain what is meant by the image of a business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the explanation:
• The image of a business is the way the business wants to be perceived by its customers.

subQuestions.questionText: From the extract on e-professionalism, identify the term that is used to describe acceptable online behaviour.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Netiquette / e-professionalism.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE consequence for a business if it disregards the importance of its professional online presence.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for one well-discussed consequence:
• The customers will lose confidence and loyalty and take their business elsewhere.
• The business will lose customers and income.
• Customers may look for another business where they can spend their money.
• Customers will look for a business that meets their expectations in terms of professionalism, quality service and customer care.
• Negative / bad publicity.
• Additional expenses will be incurred for marketing to off-set the negative publicity.

subQuestions.questionText: In the 'Social Media Dispute' scenario, explain how Mr Williams was in violation of the hotel's social media policy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the explanation (any of the following):
• He tarnished the image of the business with his adverse comments on social media.
• He negatively influenced other fellow workers.
• He bullied and harassed a colleague.

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Williams' social media friend (work colleague) reported his posts to the hotel management. If you had been in the same position at work, would you also have reported Mr Williams' conduct? Choose from YES or NO. Give TWO reasons for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-explained reason (2 x 2 = 4 marks). No marks are awarded for YES or NO on its own.
YES:
• As an employee, I am co-responsible to protect the image of the business and the personal information of fellow workers.
• I would play a role in ensuring the profitability of the business.
• If I do not report the colleague's conduct, I might be perceived as agreeing with him, giving me a bad reputation at work.
• Mr Williams bullied and harassed his colleague despite having no proof it was him who reported it.
OR NO:
• Mr Williams practised his right to freedom of speech.
• The social media page belongs to Mr Williams — he can post whatever he wants.
• Fearful of victimisation at work and on social media.

subQuestions.questionText: The value of a code of conduct is to create a cooperative, collaborative atmosphere that promotes integrity in the workplace. Explain THREE ways in which the hotel's code of conduct served its purpose in the scenario.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-explained way (3 x 2 = 6 marks). Dismissing Mr Williams on the grounds of violating the code of conduct ensures that:
• The professionalism and integrity of the hotel is protected.
• It allowed the hotel to discipline employees within a legal framework.
• Other employees are protected from repeated verbal personal attacks.
• It keeps employees accountable for their actions.
• The contravention of the code of conduct can be addressed by written warnings.
• Correct labour practices are followed by the business.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the pillar of the triple bottom line practised by RAIN, the international beverage company in the extract.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Social / Community / People pillar.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why this initiative could be considered the beverage company's CSI (corporate social investment) initiative.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the explanation:
• RAIN uses a portion of its profit to better the lives of people in communities all over the world.
Note: Accept examples of CSI initiatives.

subQuestions.questionText: The beverage company focuses on THREE key areas in their RAIN Water for Schools initiative in South Africa. In a paragraph, discuss the benefits of these key areas for the schools. Your paragraph must include: Provide clean drinking water; Sanitation facilities; Hygiene education.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the benefits of each key area (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
Provide clean drinking water:
• Many schools in South Africa do not have running water; the initiative brought drinking water to the schools, encouraging learners to drink enough water as part of a healthy lifestyle.
• Values are instilled to act responsibly by saving water; prevents diseases such as cholera and COVID-19.
Sanitation facilities:
• Schools can now have flushable toilets and hand-washing facilities.
• Having running water on the premises allows for further improvements of infrastructure.
Hygiene education:
• Learners are educated on personal hygiene practices and how sanitation facilities have to be utilised.
• Education on the responsible use of water and on observing strict hygienic practices when preparing and serving food.
Note: Focus areas can be included in any order.

subQuestions.questionText: Give your opinion on why the beverage company built 5 000 hand-washing stations during the Covid-19 pandemic, as opposed to simply handing out sanitisers to communities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the opinion:
• Building 5 000 hand-washing stations is a more sustainable initiative, as it will last for many years.
• The hand sanitisers would only offer a short-term solution, after which the protection of communities would be compromised.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the TBCSA's Covid-19 protocols for the tourism industry. Name the type of unforeseen occurrence caused by Covid-19.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Diseases / pandemic / global pandemic.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the TBCSA had to specify these protocols for tourism businesses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the explanation:
• In the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic, the TBCSA had to ensure that, while supporting tourism businesses from the negative impact of the crisis, they also ensured adherence to government's policies.
• TBCSA developed a general protocol for all tourism sectors and businesses in keeping with the government's mandate to stop the spread of the disease.
• The standardised policy was developed to provide guidance and support for the industry to move forward amidst the crisis while still protecting the sector.

subQuestions.questionText: Name FOUR protocols in the information that would impact the staff at tourism businesses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for each correct protocol (4 marks). Any FOUR of:
• A designated health and safety officer must be appointed.
• Staff will have to undergo training and be informed on Covid-19 safety practices for themselves and customers.
• Staff will have to abide by physical distancing standards.
• All staff will have to ensure they wear proper PPE.
• Staff will have to ensure they have their temperatures checked (temperature monitoring) on entrance to their workplace.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways in which the protocol of access and capacity controls (compulsory screening and limiting numbers) had negative consequences for the accommodation sector.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-discussed way (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
• Compulsory screening for all guests would have been time-consuming and costly, as it required purchasing specific equipment and training of staff.
• Capacity controls resulted in a limited number of guests, halving the profit margin of the establishment.
• Small accommodation establishments such as B&Bs and Airbnbs chose to temporarily shut down.
• Staff was retrenched or took a cut in salary.
• The inconvenience of screening protocols and safety concerns had negative cost implications for the accommodation establishment.

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why host countries insist on proof of a negative Covid-19 test result before allowing tourists to enter their country.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-explained reason (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
• It ensures that people are neither the carriers nor the source of the spread of the virus, because they have evidence of a negative Covid-19 test result.
• Host countries feel confident to allow inbound tourists with a negative test result to move freely without spreading the virus.
• Tourists with proof of a negative result will be allowed access to tourism products, services and destinations of the host country without spreading the virus.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the information on South Africa's foreign tourist arrivals (January to March, 2020 versus 2019). Identify the trend in all the inbound tourist markets in South Africa in 2020. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Decline / negative decrease in all inbound tourists to South Africa in the year 2020.

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph, recommend FOUR ways in which SATourism can rejuvenate and reignite the tourism industry to recover from the Covid-19 crisis.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each well-recommended way (4 x 2 = 8 marks):
• A partnership between government and the tourism industry to address all aspects of the recovery plan.
• Government and commercial banks making funds available for tourism businesses to apply for, in order to protect tourism assets and core infrastructure.
• Introduce safety protocols for the industry to rebuild tourism confidence.
• Negotiate with countries to open borders and air routes to reconnect South Africa to the world.
• Closely monitor and advertise the decrease in Covid-19 infections and current lockdown levels to stimulate travel.
• Continue tourism safety programmes in partnership with the police and relevant stakeholders.
• Encourage domestic travel and experiences by offering innovative, affordable packages.
• Form partnerships with neighbouring countries to promote a seamless SADC visitor experience.
• Use various opportunities for marketing South Africa both locally and internationally.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the application (app) in the picture that will be useful to customers during Covid-19 conditions. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• Eat Safe Certification Programme and Screening App.
Note: Accept only the full name.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why tourists will react positively to the app named in QUESTION 10.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for the explanation:
• Use of the screening app will reassure tourists that the places on the app will be safe and that all Covid-19 protocols will be in place.
